english_draft: NVIDIA reported record Q4 FY2026 revenue of $68.1B. The quarter ended January 25, 2026. Revenue rose 20% sequentially and 73% year over year. Data Center revenue was a record $62.3B. It rose 22% sequentially and 75% year over year. Full-year FY2026 revenue was $215.9B, up 65%. GAAP diluted EPS was $1.76. Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $1.62. GAAP gross margin was 75.0%. Non-GAAP gross margin was 75.2%. Data Center drove growth. CEO Jensen Huang cited agentic AI inflection and Grace Blackwell with NVLink as the inference platform. Q4 GAAP net income was $42.96B. The figure included other income, net of $5.604B. Non-GAAP net income was $39.55B. The difference was mainly stock-based compensation. The company issued Q1 FY2027 revenue guidance of $78.0B plus or minus 2%. The outlook excludes Data Center compute revenue from China. Q1 GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin guidance was 74.9% and 75.0%, plus or minus 50 basis points. GAAP and non-GAAP operating expense guidance was about $7.7B and $7.5B. Both figures include $1.9B of stock-based compensation. Beginning in Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA will include stock-based compensation in non-GAAP measures. Gaming revenue was $3.7B. It rose 47% year over year and fell 13% sequentially. Professional Visualization revenue was $1.3B. It rose 74% sequentially and 159% year over year. Automotive revenue was $604M. It rose 2% sequentially and 6% year over year. No preview existed before this report. The available historical reconstruction was written after the fact and cannot be used as a forecast check. Margin comparison was not direct in the source. Gross margin rose about 1.6 points sequentially under GAAP and non-GAAP. Net income per diluted share accelerated from $1.30 to $1.76 on a GAAP basis. Non-GAAP diluted EPS rose from $1.30 to $1.62. The most important next-quarter check is whether Data Center revenue can sustain quarterly growth. The second check is the impact of excluding China. The third check is the new non-GAAP treatment of stock-based compensation. The company returned $41.1B to shareholders during fiscal 2026. The remaining share repurchase authorization was $58.5B at quarter end. The next quarterly cash dividend will be $0.01 per share. The record date is March 11, 2026. The payment date is April 1, 2026.
reader_questions: If the company did not disclose Q4 FY2026 revenue guidance or a first-quarter outlook in the source, can the $78.0 billion figure be treated as actual reported guidance?
Does the $42.96 billion GAAP net income include the $5.604 billion other income, and would the non-GAAP net income of $39.55 billion be a more stable measure for trend analysis?
If no contemporaneous preview existed, why would a historical reconstruction written after the release be mentioned in the final markdown?
fact_checks: Fact-check 1: Confirmed quarter end is January 25, 2026. The source states 'fourth quarter ended January 25, 2026'.
Fact-check 2: Confirmed Q4 FY2026 revenue of $68,127 million. The source states $68.1 billion, up 20% from Q3 and up 73% from a year ago.
Fact-check 3: Confirmed Q4 Data Center revenue of $62.3 billion. The source states $62.3 billion, up 22% from Q3 and up 75% from a year ago.
Fact-check 4: Confirmed FY2026 revenue of $215.9 billion. The source states $215.9 billion, up 65% from a year ago.
Fact-check 5: Confirmed Q4 GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins of 75.0% and 75.2%. The source states 75.0% and 75.2%, respectively.
Fact-check 6: Confirmed Q4 GAAP and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.76 and $1.62. The source states $1.76 and $1.62, respectively.
Fact-check 7: Confirmed Q1 FY2027 revenue guidance of $78.0 billion plus or minus 2%. The source states this guidance.
Fact-check 8: Confirmed China is excluded from Data Center compute revenue in the Q1 outlook. The source states 'NVIDIA is not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China in its outlook.'
Fact-check 9: Confirmed the non-GAAP change beginning in Q1 FY2027. The source states NVIDIA will include stock-based compensation in non-GAAP financial measures.
